_meta.purpose: Rule-ID -> baseline-severity seed. Checkov's community edition emits NO severity (verified: all 1317 Terraform resource checks in checkov 3.2.500 return severity=None; severity is a Bridgecrew/Prisma paid-platform feature). Severity feeds priorityScore -> isQuickWin -> the --severity floor -> CI exit codes -> SARIF security-severity. Without this file the product's entire ranking spine is null.
_meta.governance: STATIC, CHECKED-IN, HUMAN-REVIEWED DATA. The model NEVER generates a baseline severity at runtime. The LLM may adjust a seed by at most +/-1 level, and only with severityAdjustedFrom plus a written justification -- it must adjust a REAL SEED, never invent one. A rule with no entry here resolves to the explicit sentinel 'unmapped'. It is NEVER defaulted to a middle value. Silence is safer than a guess.

sources.checkov-metadata: Checkov's own rule metadata. Yields nothing: OSS Checkov populates no severity on any check. Retained in the schema so that a future Checkov release, or a Prisma-licensed run, can be distinguished from our judgment.
sources.prowler: Vendor-assigned Severity from the installed Prowler check metadata (prowler 5.x, providers/aws/services/**/*.metadata.json -- 578 AWS checks). Concept-matched to the Checkov rule; the matched Prowler check ID is named in every rationale so a reviewer can verify the match.
sources.curated: Human judgment, reasoned from real AWS impact, where no authority covers the concept or where we deliberately deviate from one. SCRUTINIZE THESE HARDEST -- the rationale states the reasoning and any authority we overrode.

_meta.corpusCoverage: All 57 rule IDs that fire across the 5 Terraform fixtures (159 findings, checkov 3.3.25; was 56/158 on 3.2.500) are seeded, plus the well-known AWS criticals that do not fire on this corpus but must never resolve to 'unmapped' in a real repo.

gate1.note: Baseline severities are checked-in, human-reviewed data. The model never generates a baseline severity at runtime; it may only adjust a real seed +/-1 with a written reason. Unmapped is stated plainly, never defaulted. NOTE: the GATE-1 sign-off covers the AWS (CKV_AWS_*/CKV_SECRET_*) seeds only, NOT the CKV_K8S_* block below.

kubernetesSeeds.note: The 15 CKV_K8S_* / CKV2_K8S_* seeds carry source='curated' and pendingGate1Review=true. They are hand-curated from the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark impact model for the security-meaningful rules that fire on tests/fixtures/k8s-01-workloads. They are NOT yet human-reviewed and must be signed off exactly like the AWS seeds were. The six availability/reliability rules that also fire (CKV_K8S_8/9 probes, CKV_K8S_10/11/12/13 cpu+mem requests/limits) are DELIBERATELY left unmapped -- their severity is genuinely debatable and they are hygiene, not a security posture.

_meta.checkovGradedNote: Seeds are graded against checkov 3.3.25 (re-graded 2026-10-06 from 3.2.500; requirements.txt is a floor, checkov>=3.3.25). The corpus is now 57 rule IDs / 159 Terraform findings (CKV_AWS_394 fires once, on tf-01/main.tf). No rule disappeared between 3.2.500 and 3.3.25.

proposedSeeds2026-10-06.note: The two CKV_AWS_* rules new in checkov 3.3.x carry source='curated', pendingGate1Review=true and proposed='2026-10-06'. The file's `source` field is an authority enum validated by findings.SeverityMap, so the proposal marker is the separate `proposed` field, following the kubernetesSeeds convention. Neither rule has a Prowler analog (both are IaC-structure checks).
proposedSeeds2026-10-06.reviewChecklist: Confirm: CKV_AWS_394 (unpinned aws_availability_zones data source) = low, a determinism/change-control concern, not exposure; CKV_AWS_393 (GitHub Actions OIDC trust policy on aws_iam_role) = high, mirrors CKV_AWS_358 and an unconditioned OIDC trust lets any GitHub repository assume the role. It evaluates all 15 roles on the corpus and passes on every one.
proposedSeeds2026-10-06.alsoAdded: CKV2_AWS_61 and CKV2_AWS_64 fire only on the new tf-06-hardened-three-tier fixture (added with the threat-model skill), so they were unseeded until 2026-10-06; same proposed/pendingGate1Review convention.

CKV_K8S_16.rationale: Privileged container (CIS Kubernetes; Checkov `kubernetes`). A privileged container runs with all capabilities and host device access -- container escape to node root is trivial. Highest-consensus critical in the K8s corpus. Seeded critical.

CKV_K8S_17.rationale: Container shares the host PID namespace (hostPID). Grants visibility into and signalling of every process on the node -- a strong escape/credential-theft aid. Seeded high.

CKV_K8S_19.rationale: Container shares the host network namespace (hostNetwork). Binds host interfaces, can sniff node traffic, and bypasses NetworkPolicy entirely. Seeded high.

CKV_K8S_20.rationale: allowPrivilegeEscalation is not disabled. Lets a process gain more privileges than its parent (setuid/setgid), the mechanism behind most in-container privesc. Seeded high.

CKV_K8S_23.rationale: Root container (runAsNonRoot not enforced / runAsUser 0). Root inside the container plus any escape is root on the node; also defeats most other hardening. Seeded high.

CKV_K8S_22.rationale: Root filesystem is not read-only. A writable rootfs eases malware persistence and binary tampering. Defense-in-depth; seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_28.rationale: Container may hold the NET_RAW capability. Enables raw sockets -- ARP/DNS spoofing and packet crafting from the pod. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_37.rationale: Container is granted (or not restricted from) Linux capabilities. Extra capabilities broaden the escape surface; the guidance is to drop ALL and add back the minimum. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_31.rationale: No seccomp profile (docker/default or runtime/default) is set. Without seccomp the container has the full syscall surface, widening kernel-exploit reach. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_29.rationale: No securityContext applied to the pod/containers. Absent a securityContext the workload runs with permissive defaults and none of the above controls. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_38.rationale: Service Account token is auto-mounted where it may not be needed. A mounted SA token is a live API credential usable for lateral movement if the pod is compromised. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_14.rationale: Image tag is `latest`/blank (mutable). A mutable tag makes the running image non-reproducible and unverifiable, and silently changes on restart -- a supply-chain and rollback hazard. Seeded medium.

CKV2_K8S_6.rationale: Pod has no associated NetworkPolicy. Without one the pod sits on a flat, default-allow network -- any compromised neighbour can reach it. Seeded medium.

CKV_K8S_43.rationale: Image is not pinned by digest. The stronger form of the mutable-tag problem; seeded low as defense-in-depth beyond CKV_K8S_14.

CKV_K8S_40.rationale: Container may run as a low UID that can collide with a host user. Host-UID-collision hardening; low impact on its own. Seeded low.

CKV_AWS_338.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): raised low->medium to match Prowler's analog. Also the most frequent rule on the corpus (11x); at `low` it would have been invisible under the default --severity medium floor, silently hiding the single most common finding the product emits.

CKV_AWS_158.rationale: CloudWatch log group not encrypted with KMS. Logs routinely contain tokens, request bodies, and PII. Prowler: cloudwatch_log_group_kms_encryption_enabled = medium.

CKV2_AWS_62.rationale: S3 bucket has no event notifications. Detection/response gap -- object-level changes go unobserved. Prowler: s3_bucket_event_notifications_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_18.rationale: S3 access logging absent -- detection gap, not direct exposure. You cannot investigate an incident on a bucket with no access log. Prowler: s3_bucket_server_access_logging_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_144.rationale: S3 cross-region replication disabled. Durability/DR control; no confidentiality or integrity impact. Prowler: s3_bucket_cross_region_replication = low.

CKV_AWS_130.rationale: Subnet assigns public IPs by default -- every instance launched into it lands on the internet unless explicitly overridden. Prowler: vpc_subnet_no_public_ip_by_default = medium.

CKV_AWS_355.rationale: IAM policy uses "*" as the resource for restrictable actions. Unconstrained resource scope is the standard precondition for lateral movement and data access beyond intent. Prowler rates the adjacent concepts high (iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation, iam_inline_policy_no_administrative_privileges); no exact analog exists, so this is our call.

CKV_AWS_117.rationale: Lambda not configured inside a VPC. Defense-in-depth / egress-control gap; a non-VPC Lambda is not itself reachable from the internet. Prowler: awslambda_function_inside_vpc = low.

CKV_AWS_116.rationale: Lambda has no dead-letter queue. Reliability and observability control -- failed invocations are lost silently. No security exposure. No Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_173.rationale: Lambda environment variables not encrypted with a KMS CMK. Env vars are where function secrets live; at rest they are AWS-key encrypted but readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. Matches the infrabot fixture answer key (SECURITY_FLAWS.md TF-02 #5 = MEDIUM). Distinct from CKV_AWS_45, which detects secrets actually present.

CKV_AWS_272.rationale: Lambda code-signing not configured. Supply-chain integrity control -- valuable but rarely adopted, and its absence does not itself expose anything. No Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_115.rationale: Lambda has no reserved concurrency limit. Availability/blast-radius control (one function can exhaust account concurrency); not a confidentiality or integrity issue. No Prowler analog.

CKV2_AWS_53.rationale: API Gateway request validation not enabled. Defense-in-depth: pushes malformed input to the backend, which should be validating anyway. Not an exposure on its own. No Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_260.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): reviewed and HELD at medium. Two authorities conflict (Prowler high, fixture answer key low for the analogous 443 rule); medium is the deliberate reconciliation. Security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to port 80. Deliberately seeded BELOW Prowler's ec2_securitygroup_allow_ingress_from_internet_to_any_port (high): port 80 on a public web tier is frequently intentional, and the infrabot fixture answer key rates the analogous internet-open 443 rule LOW. Medium splits the difference -- cleartext HTTP from the internet is a real transport-security finding, but it is not the SSH/RDP/database exposure that earns a high. TWO AUTHORITIES CONFLICT HERE; this is our reconciliation.

CKV_AWS_195.rationale: Glue component has no security configuration -- job bookmarks, CloudWatch logs, and S3 targets are written unencrypted. Prowler rates the Glue encryption family medium (glue_etl_jobs_cloudwatch_logs_encryption_enabled, glue_etl_jobs_job_bookmark_encryption_enabled, glue_ml_transform_encrypted_at_rest).

CKV_AWS_300.rationale: S3 lifecycle does not abort incomplete multipart uploads. Cost and storage hygiene; no security impact. Prowler: s3_bucket_lifecycle_enabled = low.

CKV_AWS_290.rationale: IAM policy grants write access without constraints. Unconstrained write is the direct precondition for privilege escalation and destructive action. Prowler rates the family high (iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation, iam_inline_policy_no_administrative_privileges).

CKV_AWS_288.rationale: IAM policy permits data exfiltration (unconstrained read/copy across services). Prowler has no exfiltration-specific check; seeded high to match the rest of the unconstrained-IAM family, since the outcome is bulk data loss.

CKV_AWS_21.rationale: S3 bucket versioning disabled -- no recovery from overwrite or ransomware-style deletion. Prowler: s3_bucket_object_versioning = medium.

CKV_AWS_145.rationale: S3 bucket not encrypted with a KMS CMK (AES256/SSE-S3 only). Loses key-usage audit and revocation. Prowler: s3_bucket_kms_encryption = medium.

CKV_AWS_163.rationale: ECR image scanning on push disabled -- vulnerable images ship undetected. Prowler: ecr_repositories_scan_images_on_push_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_136.rationale: ECR repository not encrypted with a KMS CMK. ECR is AES256-encrypted by default, so this is a key-custody upgrade, not the absence of encryption. Seeded consistently with the rest of the CMK-instead-of-AWS-key family (all medium in Prowler). No exact Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_51.rationale: ECR image tags are mutable -- a deployed tag can be silently repointed at different code. Supply-chain integrity. Prowler: ecr_repositories_tag_immutability = medium.

CKV_AWS_150.rationale: Load balancer has no deletion protection. Availability control. Prowler: elbv2_deletion_protection = medium.

CKV_AWS_131.rationale: ALB does not drop invalid HTTP headers -- enables request smuggling / desync attacks against the backend. Prowler: elbv2_desync_mitigation_mode = medium.

CKV_AWS_2.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): raised medium->high. Cleartext credentials and session tokens crossing the public internet is a real exposure, not a hygiene gap. Overrides Prowler/FSBP deliberately.

CKV_AWS_378.rationale: Load balancer target group uses HTTP to the backend. This is LB-to-target traffic inside the VPC, not internet-facing -- materially lower than the cleartext frontend listener (CKV_AWS_2). Seeded one level below it. No Prowler analog.

CKV2_AWS_12.rationale: Default security group does not restrict all traffic. Anything launched without an explicit SG inherits it; CIS AWS 5.3. Prowler: ec2_securitygroup_default_restrict_traffic = high.

CKV2_AWS_20.rationale: ALB does not redirect HTTP to HTTPS -- clients that arrive on :80 stay in cleartext. Prowler: elbv2_ssl_listeners = medium.

CKV2_AWS_28.rationale: Public-facing ALB not protected by a WAF. Prowler: elbv2_waf_acl_attached = medium.

CKV_AWS_103.rationale: Load balancer permits TLS below 1.2 -- downgrade and known-cipher attacks. Prowler: elbv2_insecure_ssl_ciphers = medium.

CKV_AWS_289.rationale: IAM policy allows permissions management / resource exposure without constraints (iam:Put*Policy, *:PutResourcePolicy). A principal that can rewrite policy can grant itself anything. Prowler: iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation = high.

CKV_AWS_26.rationale: SNS topic not encrypted at rest. Prowler: sns_topics_kms_encryption_at_rest_enabled = high. (Higher than the other at-rest-encryption seeds; taken from the authority as-is -- SNS payloads frequently carry alerts and PII in transit-adjacent storage.)

CKV_AWS_316.rationale: CodeBuild project runs in privileged mode -- a compromised or malicious build escapes the container and takes the build host, including its role credentials. Prowler's closest concept, ecs_task_definitions_no_privileged_containers, is high. No exact CodeBuild analog.

CKV_AWS_147.rationale: CodeBuild project artifacts/logs not encrypted with a CMK. Build artifacts leak source and secrets. Prowler: codebuild_report_group_export_encrypted = medium.

CKV_AWS_91.rationale: ELBv2 access logging disabled -- no record of who hit the front door. Prowler: elbv2_logging_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_79.rationale: IMDSv1 still enabled. The single most-exploited AWS misconfiguration: any SSRF in an app on the instance reads the instance role's credentials. Prowler: ec2_instance_imdsv2_enabled = high and ec2_launch_template_imdsv2_required = high. Matches the fixture answer key (SECURITY_FLAWS.md TF-01 #2 = HIGH).

CKV_AWS_161.rationale: RDS IAM database authentication not enabled -- long-lived static DB passwords instead of short-lived IAM tokens. Prowler: rds_instance_iam_authentication_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_354.rationale: RDS Performance Insights not encrypted with a CMK. Performance Insights retains query text, which can embed literal values from application data. Consistent with the CMK family (Prowler rates RDS encryption checks medium). No exact Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_293.rationale: Database instance has no deletion protection. Availability/durability. Prowler: rds_instance_deletion_protection = medium.

CKV_AWS_16.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): raised medium->high, overriding Prowler/FSBP RDS.3 to match infrabot's fixture answer key (SECURITY_FLAWS.md TF-01 #1), which WS-8 grades detection recall against. Unencrypted RDS at rest is conventionally a high; seed and answer key must not disagree.

CKV2_AWS_69.rationale: RDS not configured to require encryption in transit. Database credentials and query results cross the network in cleartext. Prowler: rds_instance_transport_encrypted = high.

CKV_AWS_237.rationale: API Gateway REST API lacks create_before_destroy. A Terraform lifecycle/availability concern during replacement. No security impact whatsoever -- seeded informational rather than inflated so it does not compete with real findings.

CKV_AWS_120.rationale: API Gateway caching not enabled. Performance and cost; no security impact. (Distinct from CKV_AWS_276/CKV_AWS_225, which concern what the cache stores and logs.) Surfaced for completeness only.

CKV_AWS_76.rationale: API Gateway access logging disabled -- no request-level audit trail for the public API surface. Prowler: apigateway_restapi_logging_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_276.rationale: API Gateway method settings enable data trace, which writes full request/response payloads -- including auth headers and PII -- into CloudWatch logs. Prowler's nearest concept, cloudwatch_log_group_no_secrets_in_logs, is medium.

CKV_AWS_225.rationale: API Gateway method-level caching not enabled. Performance control; no security impact. Same reasoning as CKV_AWS_120.

CKV_AWS_287.rationale: IAM policy allows credentials exposure (e.g. unconstrained iam:CreateAccessKey, sts:AssumeRole, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on *). Direct path to durable credential theft. No exact Prowler analog; seeded to match the unconstrained-IAM family, which Prowler rates high.

CKV_AWS_119.rationale: DynamoDB table not encrypted with a KMS CMK. Prowler: dynamodb_tables_kms_cmk_encryption_enabled = medium. Matches the fixture answer key (SECURITY_FLAWS.md TF-02 #2 = MEDIUM).

CKV2_AWS_31.rationale: WAFv2 web ACL has no logging configuration -- blocked-request evidence is not retained. Prowler: wafv2_webacl_logging_enabled = medium.

CKV2_AWS_51.rationale: API Gateway does not use client certificate authentication to the backend, so the backend cannot verify the request came from API Gateway. Prowler: apigateway_restapi_client_certificate_enabled = medium.

CKV2_AWS_77.rationale: API Gateway's attached WAFv2 web ACL has no AWS Managed Rules. A WAF with no rule groups is decorative. Prowler: apigateway_restapi_waf_acl_attached = medium.

CKV_AWS_159.rationale: Athena workgroup does not enforce query-result encryption -- result sets from an encrypted lake land unencrypted in S3. Prowler: athena_workgroup_encryption = medium.

CKV2_AWS_71.rationale: ACM certificate uses a wildcard domain. Widens blast radius if the private key is compromised, but a wildcard cert is a deliberate and extremely common architecture choice. No Prowler analog (its ACM checks cover expiry and key algorithm).

CKV2_AWS_11.rationale: VPC flow logging not enabled. Network-level forensics are impossible after the fact. CIS AWS 3.9. Prowler: vpc_flow_logs_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_219.rationale: CodePipeline artifact store not using a KMS CMK. Pipeline artifacts routinely contain source and build secrets. Consistent with codebuild_report_group_export_encrypted (Prowler = medium); no exact CodePipeline analog.

CKV_AWS_20.rationale: S3 bucket grants READ to everyone. Public data exposure -- the archetypal cloud breach. Prowler: s3_bucket_public_list_acl = critical.

CKV_AWS_57.rationale: S3 bucket grants WRITE to everyone. Anyone on the internet can overwrite objects -- content injection, malware hosting, destruction. Prowler: s3_bucket_public_write_acl = critical.

CKV_AWS_70.rationale: S3 bucket policy allows an action with any Principal. Prowler: s3_bucket_public_access = critical.

CKV_AWS_375.rationale: S3 bucket has global view ACL permissions. Prowler: s3_bucket_public_list_acl = critical.

CKV_AWS_53.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): lowered high->medium, deferring to Prowler's bucket-level PAB rating. A missing guardrail is not itself an exposure: if a bucket is actually public, that fires its own critical/high finding, so seeding PAB high double-counts the same risk.

CKV_AWS_54.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): lowered high->medium. Same reasoning as CKV_AWS_53.

CKV_AWS_55.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): lowered high->medium. Same reasoning as CKV_AWS_53.

CKV_AWS_56.rationale: GATE 1 (human review, 2026-07-13): lowered high->medium. Same reasoning as CKV_AWS_53.

CKV_AWS_19.rationale: S3 bucket not encrypted at rest. Prowler: s3_bucket_default_encryption = medium.

CKV_AWS_379.rationale: S3 bucket has no secure-transport (aws:SecureTransport) policy -- objects may be fetched over plain HTTP. Prowler: s3_bucket_secure_transport_policy = medium.

CKV_AWS_24.rationale: Security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 (SSH). Prowler: ec2_securitygroup_allow_ingress_from_internet_to_tcp_port_22 = high.

CKV_AWS_25.rationale: Security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389 (RDP). Prowler: ec2_securitygroup_allow_ingress_from_internet_to_tcp_port_3389 = high.

CKV_AWS_277.rationale: Security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to port -1, i.e. ALL ports open to the internet. Prowler: ec2_securitygroup_allow_ingress_from_internet_to_all_ports = critical.

CKV_AWS_382.rationale: Security group allows unrestricted egress to all ports. Egress filtering is a genuine exfiltration control, but wide-open egress is the AWS default and near-universal; seeded low so it does not drown the ingress findings that actually let attackers in. No Prowler analog.

CKV_AWS_23.rationale: Security group or rule has no description. Documentation hygiene; zero security impact. Seeded informational rather than low to keep it out of the way.

CKV_AWS_17.rationale: RDS instance is publicly accessible. A database with a public endpoint is one credential away from total data loss. Prowler: rds_instance_no_public_access = critical.

CKV_AWS_302.rationale: DB snapshot is public -- a full copy of the database, restorable by anyone. Prowler: rds_snapshots_public_access = critical.

CKV_AWS_41.rationale: Hard-coded AWS access key and secret key in a provider block. Long-lived root-adjacent credentials committed to source control. Prowler's analogous secret-in-source check (codebuild_project_source_repo_url_no_sensitive_credentials) is critical.

CKV_AWS_45.rationale: Hard-coded secrets in Lambda environment variables. Prowler: awslambda_function_no_secrets_in_variables = critical.

CKV_AWS_46.rationale: Hard-coded secrets in EC2 user data. User data is readable by anything that can reach IMDS on the instance. Prowler: awslambda_function_no_secrets_in_code = critical (same concept: a secret literal committed into deployable code).

CKV_AWS_301.rationale: Lambda function is publicly accessible (resource policy allows any principal to invoke). Prowler: awslambda_function_not_publicly_accessible = critical.

CKV_AWS_32.rationale: ECR repository policy is public -- anyone can pull (and, with write, poison) your container images. Prowler: ecr_repositories_not_publicly_accessible = critical.

CKV_AWS_168.rationale: SQS queue policy is public. Prowler: sqs_queues_not_publicly_accessible = critical.

CKV_AWS_169.rationale: SNS topic policy is public. Prowler: sns_topics_not_publicly_accessible = high.

CKV_AWS_27.rationale: SQS queue not encrypted at rest. Prowler: sqs_queues_server_side_encryption_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_49.rationale: IAM policy document allows "*" as a statement's actions. Unbounded action scope. Prowler: iam_aws_attached_policy_no_administrative_privileges / iam_inline_policy_no_administrative_privileges = high.

CKV_AWS_62.rationale: IAM policy grants full "*:*" administrative privileges. Prowler: iam_aws_attached_policy_no_administrative_privileges = high.

CKV_AWS_63.rationale: IAM policy document allows "*" as a statement's actions. Same family as CKV_AWS_49. Prowler: iam_inline_policy_no_administrative_privileges = high.

CKV_AWS_274.rationale: Role, user, or group uses the AWS AdministratorAccess managed policy. Prowler: iam_role_administratoraccess_policy = high.

CKV_AWS_60.rationale: IAM role trust policy does not restrict who may assume it. A wildcard principal on an assume-role policy is an account takeover primitive. Prowler: iam_no_custom_policy_permissive_role_assumption = high.

CKV_AWS_61.rationale: IAM policy allows assume-role across all services/principals. Prowler: iam_no_custom_policy_permissive_role_assumption = high.

CKV_AWS_286.rationale: IAM policy allows privilege escalation. Prowler: iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation = high.

CKV_AWS_107.rationale: IAM policy document allows credentials exposure. aws_iam_policy_document twin of CKV_AWS_287; same severity for the same reason.

CKV_AWS_108.rationale: IAM policy document allows data exfiltration. aws_iam_policy_document twin of CKV_AWS_288; same severity for the same reason.

CKV_AWS_109.rationale: IAM policy document allows permissions management / resource exposure without constraints. aws_iam_policy_document twin of CKV_AWS_289. Prowler: iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation = high.

CKV_AWS_110.rationale: IAM policy document allows privilege escalation. aws_iam_policy_document twin of CKV_AWS_286. Prowler: iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation = high.

CKV_AWS_111.rationale: IAM policy document allows write access without constraints. aws_iam_policy_document twin of CKV_AWS_290. Prowler: iam_policy_allows_privilege_escalation = high.

CKV_AWS_7.rationale: Customer-managed KMS key does not have rotation enabled. Prowler: kms_cmk_rotation_enabled = high.

CKV_AWS_33.rationale: KMS key policy contains a wildcard (*) principal -- anyone can use the key, which defeats every at-rest encryption control that depends on it. Prowler: kms_key_not_publicly_accessible = critical.

CKV_AWS_35.rationale: CloudTrail logs not encrypted at rest with a KMS CMK. Prowler: cloudtrail_kms_encryption_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_36.rationale: CloudTrail log file validation disabled -- tampering with the audit trail becomes undetectable. Prowler: cloudtrail_log_file_validation_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_67.rationale: CloudTrail is not enabled in all regions -- activity in unmonitored regions is invisible, which is exactly where attackers operate. Prowler: cloudtrail_multi_region_enabled = high.

CKV_AWS_28.rationale: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery disabled. Prowler: dynamodb_tables_pitr_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_38.rationale: EKS public endpoint accessible from 0.0.0.0/0. Prowler: eks_cluster_not_publicly_accessible = high.

CKV_AWS_39.rationale: EKS public endpoint enabled. Prowler: eks_cluster_not_publicly_accessible = high.

CKV_AWS_58.rationale: EKS cluster secrets not encrypted with a KMS CMK -- Kubernetes Secrets sit in etcd under the AWS-managed key only. Prowler: eks_cluster_kms_cmk_encryption_in_secrets_enabled = medium.

CKV_AWS_88.rationale: EC2 instance has a public IP. Prowler: ec2_instance_public_ip = medium.

CKV_AWS_87.rationale: Redshift cluster is publicly accessible. Prowler: redshift_cluster_public_access = high.

CKV_AWS_149.rationale: Secrets Manager secret not encrypted with a KMS CMK. Prowler rates the Secrets Manager hygiene family medium (secretsmanager_automatic_rotation_enabled, secretsmanager_secret_rotated_periodically); the secret is still encrypted under the AWS-managed key, so this is key custody, not exposure.

CKV_AWS_333.rationale: ECS service assigns public IPs to tasks automatically. Prowler: ecs_service_no_assign_public_ip = high.

CKV_AWS_334.rationale: ECS container runs privileged -- container escape to the host and its instance role. Prowler: ecs_task_definitions_no_privileged_containers = high.

CKV_AWS_335.rationale: ECS task definition shares the host namespace (pid/ipc), which collapses the container boundary. Prowler: ecs_task_definitions_host_namespace_not_shared = high.

CKV_AWS_336.rationale: ECS container filesystem is not read-only. Prowler: ecs_task_definitions_containers_readonly_access = high.

CKV_AWS_65.rationale: ECS cluster does not have Container Insights enabled. Observability/monitoring control -- no direct security exposure. Prowler: ecs_cluster_container_insights_enabled = medium; seeded one level lower because Container Insights is a metrics feature, not a security or audit control.

CKV_SECRET_4.rationale: Basic Auth credentials hardcoded in source (Checkov `secrets` framework). A committed credential is live the moment it lands in git history, readable by anyone with repo access and unremovable without history rewrite. Seeded high rather than critical because the finding is a pattern match, not proof the credential is valid/production; the LLM layer may raise it to critical when context (an `sk-prod-` prefix, a DB master user) warrants.

CKV_SECRET_6.rationale: Base64 high-entropy string hardcoded in source (Checkov `secrets` framework) -- the detector behind the three plaintext production secrets found in tf-02/lambda.tf. High, not critical, because entropy detection carries false positives (a real base64 asset can trip it); the LLM layer adjusts on context. See run_checkov secrets-framework default.

CKV_AWS_393.rationale: New in checkov 3.3.x (resource-level mirror of CKV_AWS_358). An aws_iam_role trust policy that federates GitHub Actions OIDC without a `sub` condition, or with an abusable claim, lets ANY GitHub repository assume the role -- a documented cross-tenant takeover path into the account. Not critical because exploitation needs the attacker to notice the trust and the role's own permissions bound the blast radius. No Prowler analog (IaC-structure check). Evaluated on all 15 aws_iam_role resources in the corpus and PASSED on every one; seeded so a real repo's failure never resolves to unmapped.

CKV_AWS_394.rationale: New in checkov 3.3.x. An aws_availability_zones data source with no zone-name/zone-id filter returns a set that grows when AWS adds a zone, so count-indexed subnets can drift or be re-created on a later apply. That is a determinism and change-control concern, not a confidentiality or exposure risk; informational would also be defensible. No Prowler analog (IaC-structure check). Fires once on the corpus: tf-01-three-tier-webapp/main.tf, aws_availability_zones.available.

CKV2_AWS_61.rationale: Fires on the hardened fixture tf-06 (the ALB access-log bucket has no lifecycle configuration). Missing lifecycle rules are a cost and retention-hygiene concern, not an exposure; CIS has no equivalent. Prowler analog: s3_bucket_lifecycle_enabled (informational there).

CKV2_AWS_64.rationale: Fires on the hardened fixture tf-06 (the RDS customer-managed KMS key has no key policy). Without an explicit key policy the key falls back to the account-default policy, which grants the account root full control and leaves key usage ungoverned by the IaC. A confidentiality control gap, but not an exposure by itself.
